claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances and exceeds tolerance. The trip record gives an actual route of 13.8 km against a recommended route of 12.1 km — a deviation of 1.70 km, with the recomputed within_tolerance flag reading false against POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. Because the deviation is over 1 km, the tolerance rows of POL-RD-24 — rows (c) and (e) — are both closed, and this case must land on a refund row.

The driver did not inform the rider before or at the point of deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires. The route_deviation_detected event is timed 10:21:30 and the first off-route fix is on Upper Serangoon Road at 10:21:38, while the driver's message MSG-05005-003 — which tells the rider he had gone via Upper Serangoon Road — was not sent until 10:24:30, roughly three minutes after the vehicle had already left the recommended route. The contact obligation in POL-RD-21 is therefore not met.

The counterparty statement asserts the rider was informed 'before I changed route', but that assertion is contradicted by the platform's own timestamps: deviation detected 10:21:30, driver's message sent 10:24:30. A party's account does not displace the trip record, the event log and the GPS trace that are measured against it, and no in-app call exists in the record to carry a verbal notice (in_app_calls is empty).

The rider's reply 'ok noted' at 10:25:00 does not bring this into row (a) of POL-RD-24. Row (a) requires that the rider was informed and agreed; POL-RD-21 fixes the informing as something that must happen before or at the point of deviation, and a one-word reaction to a reroute already three minutes underway is not agreement to a reroute proposed in advance. Row (a) being unavailable, the case falls to row (b) — traffic-justified but rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — which refunds the excess distance fare.

The traffic-justification question does not change the rider's entitlement, whichever way it resolves. POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window, and EV-ADVIS-05005-01 carries both intersects_route and justifies_reroute as undetermined (null, determined_by judge). If the KPE breakdown advisory is held to justify the reroute, row (b) applies because the rider was not informed in time; if it is not held to justify it, row (d) applies. Both rows award the refund of the excess distance fare in full.

The quantum is fixed by the fare model: the excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate without surge — 1.70 km x 0.92 SGD = 1.564, rounded to the cent, 1.56 SGD — and the ledger confirms the rider was charged the full metered fare at a 0.92 SGD per-km rate. That 1.56 SGD is the measure of the fare increase the rider complains of, and it is the only monetary remedy POL-RD-24 provides for a route deviation; the rider's stated claim of 5.00 SGD is not the measure the policy uses.

The present payment state must not simply stand. The ledger shows total_charged 23.04, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, and the dispute was filed by the rider. NO_ACTION is party-relative and would leave the rider carrying the whole charge, including the 1.56 SGD attributable to the deviation; a PARTIAL_REFUND of that sum is the ruling that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed excess.

No fact the refund rows need is missing or impaired, so POL-GEN-26 has nothing to escalate. Both recorded distances sit on a COMPLETE trip record at weight 1.0, the route taken and its timing are corroborated by a COMPLETE 48-fix trace at weight 1.0, and the notice timing rests on a contiguous 4-entry chat log at weight 1.0 plus the platform event log. The contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, both profiles carry fraud_flags 0, and POL-RD-25's 2 km escalation limb is switched off (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false), so an AI ruling is competent here at the 0.80 confidence the policy requires.

claims.text: The reroute is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23: EV-ADVIS-05005-01 is an LTA VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway (KPE) with valid_from 09:59:38 and valid_to 10:54:38 on 15 August 2026, a window that spans the whole trip (10:14:38 to 10:38:08, EV-TRIP-05005), and VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN is an admissible 'incident' type in POL-RD-23's traffic_justification_types, which the artifact's own justification_kind returns as 'incident'. The recommended route the driver is said to have left runs via the KPE itself (EV-TRIP-05005 optimal_route_via), so the advisory names the recommended route's own road for the segment and time the clause asks about.

The deviation is agreed on the chat log, which is what POL-RD-21 makes decisive: EV-CHAT-05005 carries MSG-05005-003 (driver, 10:24:30) giving the reason for the reroute, 'KPE got breakdown inside the tunnel so I go Upper Serangoon Road instead', and MSG-05005-004 (rider, 10:25:00) replying 'ok noted'. The rider received the notice, read it and answered it with an acknowledgment rather than an objection; POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed, and no separate recording is needed because the notice was by in-app chat.

The notice was served at the point of deviation, not after it: EV-TRIP-05005 times the departure from the recommended route at 10:21:30 and the rejoin at 10:35:21, and EV-GPS-05005 places the vehicle on Upper Serangoon Road from the 10:21:38 fix onward, so the deviation was still in progress when the driver's message was delivered at 10:24:33. POL-RD-21 requires notice 'before or at the point of deviation'; notice served while the deviation is still running satisfies that limb, and the rider's assertion that he 'had no say' is answered by his own reply on the same log.

On the POL-RD-24 matrix the only live rows are (a) and (b), because the deviation is 1.70 km (13.8 km actual less 12.1 km recommended, EV-TRIP-05005) and so is over the 1.0 km tolerance, which excludes rows (c) and (e). Row (b) requires that the rider was 'not informed', and the chat log contradicts that. POL-RD-24's escalation example, 'informed but the rider objected', does not apply either, because the rider's only response was 'ok noted'. The case therefore fits row (a): traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km, no refund, and the present charge stands.

The 5.00 SGD claimed cannot be awarded in any event: POL-RD-24 licenses only NO_ACTION, PARTIAL_REFUND and ESCALATE, and the most it can move is the excess distance fare, 1.70 km x 0.92 SGD/km = 1.56 SGD (EV-TRIP-05005 deviation distance and EV-FARE-05005 per_km_rate_sgd, which the fare ledger's own derived figure confirms). Returning the whole 5.00 SGD would be a FULL_REFUND under POL-GEN-03, and that value is not on this category's list.

Nothing suspends an AI ruling on this case: the value contested is 5.00 SGD, inside POL-GEN-22's below-10.00 SGD band, and both profiles report fraud_flags of 0 (EV-RPROF-05005, EV-DPROF-05005), so the 0.95 threshold that a fraud flag would impose is not engaged and POL-GEN-22 permits the ruling to be final at POL-RD-25's 0.80 confidence.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: part of your fare is returned. The platform trip record (EV-TRIP-05005, weight 1.0) shows the actual route was 13.8 km against a recommended 12.1 km — a deviation of 1.70 km, and the record's own within_tolerance flag reads false against POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. Because the deviation is over tolerance, POL-RD-24 does not let the tolerance rows (c) and (e) apply. The remedy POL-RD-24 gives for a deviation of this kind is the excess distance fare, and that is 1.70 km × 0.92 SGD/km = 1.56 SGD (EV-TRIP-05005 deviation distance; EV-FARE-05005 per_km_rate_sgd, confirmed by the ledger's own derived excess_distance_fare_sgd of 1.56). That 1.56 SGD is the whole of what the policy moves; your stated 5.00 SGD is not the measure POL-RD-24 uses, and returning it would be a FULL_REFUND, a value this category's clause does not license.

To the driver: I could not accept your advocate's no-refund claim. POL-RD-21 requires you to inform the rider of the deviation by in-app chat — or verbally with a recording — before or at the point of deviation. The record times the departure from the recommended route at 10:21:30 (EV-TRIP-05005 route_deviation_detected; the first off-route fix is Upper Serangoon Road at 10:21:38 on EV-GPS-05005), while your message MSG-05005-003 was sent at 10:24:30 (EV-CHAT-05005) — about three minutes after the vehicle had already left the route. The rider's 'ok noted' at 10:25:00 answers a notice given after the fact; a late notice plus a one-word acknowledgment does not meet POL-RD-21's timing limb or convert this into the 'informed and agreed' case that row (a) of POL-RD-24 requires. Row (a) is therefore unavailable and no refund is not the outcome.

On traffic justification: EV-ADVIS-05005-01 is an LTA VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN advisory on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway within the trip window (09:59:38–10:54:38), and VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN is an admissible 'incident' type under POL-RD-23. But the advisory's location is on the KPE after the Upper Paya Lebar Road exit — past the point at which the recommended route leaves the KPE for Paya Lebar Road (EV-TRIP-05005 optimal_route_via and route_rejoined event) — so on POL-RD-23 it does not intersect the recommended route and does not justify the reroute: row (d) applies. I record that this question does not change the money: if the advisory were treated as justifying the reroute, row (b) — traffic-justified but rider not informed — awards exactly the same 1.56 SGD. The rider's point that both live rows pay the same sum is correct.

On competence: the contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, both profiles show fraud_flags of 0 (EV-RPROF-05005, EV-DPROF-05005), and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false), so an AI ruling is competent; my confidence is 0.9, above the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires. No fact the refund rows need is missing or impaired, so POL-GEN-26 has nothing to escalate. No clause produces a referral here: POL-NS-24, POL-NS-25 and POL-NS-22 belong to the no-show fee rules and nothing in this route-deviation record fires them.

Rider and driver: 1.56 SGD of this trip's charge is returned to the rider. The rest of the fare stands; the 5.00 SGD asked for is not the measure this policy uses.

What the record shows. The app's recommended route was 12.1 km (Punggol Central, TPE, KPE, Paya Lebar Road); the route actually driven was 13.8 km, because the driver left the recommended route at the TPE / Upper Serangoon Road exit and ran down Upper Serangoon Road before rejoining at Paya Lebar Road. The deviation is 1.70 km (13.8 - 12.1), above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. Both distances are the platform's own recorded figures on a complete trip record (EV-TRIP-05005, weight 1.0), so the deviation is established and the tolerance rows of POL-RD-24 (rows (c) and (e)) are closed.

The informing duty. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to tell the rider of a reroute by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation. The event log in EV-TRIP-05005 times the departure from the recommended route at 10:21:30, and the driver-device trace (EV-GPS-05005, weight 1.0) places the vehicle off-route from the 10:21:38 fix. The driver's message MSG-05005-003 was sent at 10:24:30 - about three minutes after the deviation had already begun - so the notice was not given before or at the point of deviation. The rider's 'ok noted' at 10:25:00 shows he did not object, but it cannot make a late notice timely: row (a) of POL-RD-24 requires the rider to have been informed as well as agreed, and the informing limb was not met. The driver's account that he informed the passenger 'before I changed route' is contradicted by those timestamps and by the empty in-app call list, so I do not follow it. The driver's argument that notice given while the deviation was still running is notice 'at the point of deviation' is rejected: the clause fixes the point of deviation as the moment of leaving the route.

Traffic justification. The LTA record (EV-ADVIS-05005-01, weight 1.0) shows a VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN on the KPE, in the direction of travel, valid 09:59:38 to 10:54:38 on the trip date - a type POL-RD-23 admits as an 'incident' and a window that spans the trip (10:14:38-10:38:08) and lies on the KPE stretch the recommended route uses. I read that as traffic justification, which puts the case on row (b) of POL-RD-24. Even if the advisory were read as sitting past the point at which the recommended route leaves the KPE, the case would fall on row (d): both rows return the excess distance fare, so the outcome does not turn on it, nothing needs escalating under POL-GEN-26, and the rider's point that the refund is the same either way is accepted.

The amount. POL-RD-24 measures the refund as the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.70 km x 0.92 SGD/km = 1.564, rounded to the cent, 1.56 SGD (EV-FARE-05005; per_km_rate_sgd 0.92, distance_charged_km 13.8, total_charged 23.04, refund_issued_sgd 0.0, and the ledger's own derived excess_distance_fare_sgd of 1.56). The 5.00 SGD claimed is the amount asked back, not the fare attributable to the deviation, and the whole trip fare is not returnable because the rider was carried to the destination and most of the route was as recommended; a full refund is not a value this category licenses. The driver's point that the claim cannot exceed 1.56 SGD is therefore accepted as to quantum.

Confidence and who decides. The contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band; neither profile carries a fraud flag (EV-RPROF-05005, EV-DPROF-05005); and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off, so an AI ruling is competent at the 0.80 confidence this category requires. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts is at full weight (1.0), and I hold the ruling at 0.85. No clause produces a referral in this case, and no amount is due to the driver.

To both parties: the route taken was longer than the route the app recommended, and part of the extra charge is refunded — 1.56 SGD. Here is how I got there.

Deviation (both sides agree on the figure). The platform's trip record (EV-TRIP-05005) gives the recommended route as 12.1 km and the route actually driven as 13.8 km — a deviation of 1.70 km (POL-RD-22). That is more than the 1.0 km tolerance, so the 'within tolerance' rows of POL-RD-24 are closed. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05005) only shows which route was driven and when; it is not used to re-measure the distance.

Traffic justification. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05005-01) is a VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN on the KPE — the recommended route's own road — in the direction of travel, with a window (09:59:38–10:54:38) that covers the whole trip, and 'incident' types justify a reroute under POL-RD-23. I therefore treat the reroute as traffic-justified. I note the rider's point that the answer is the same either way (row (b) or row (d) of POL-RD-24 both refund the excess distance fare), so nothing turns on it.

Notice — this is what decides the case. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to tell the rider of a reroute before or at the point of deviation. The trip record times the vehicle leaving the recommended route at 10:21:30, and the GPS trace puts it off-route from 10:21:38; the driver's message (MSG-05005-003, EV-CHAT-05005) went out at 10:24:30, about three minutes after the turn had already been made. That is not before or at the point of deviation. The driver's account that he informed the rider before he changed route is contradicted by the platform's own timestamps, and there is no call recording in the record to carry a verbal notice. The case therefore falls in row (b) of POL-RD-24: traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — refund of the excess distance fare. It is not row (a): the rider's 'ok noted' came after the turn was already taken, so it is not the advance informing and agreement row (a) needs, and it does not make the deviation 'agreed' under POL-RD-21. Nor is this the 'informed but objected' case that would be escalated — there was no timely notice to object to.

Amount. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate without surge: 1.70 km x 0.92 SGD/km = 1.56 SGD (EV-TRIP-05005 deviation; EV-FARE-05005 per-km rate, whose own derived excess_distance_fare_sgd is 1.56). Rider, I cannot award the 5.00 SGD you asked for: POL-RD-24's remedy for a route deviation is the excess distance fare, and returning the whole 5.00 would be a FULL_REFUND, which this category's list does not offer.

Driver, this is not a finding about your driving — the reroute itself was justified. It is only the timing of the notice that produces the small refund.

Nothing here requires escalation. The distances, the route and the notice timing all rest on complete records at weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-05005, EV-GPS-05005, EV-CHAT-05005), the contested value is 5.00 SGD, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so an AI ruling is competent at POL-RD-25's 0.80 threshold. Confidence 0.85.
